A.explanation: Air resistance is the force of air on the firework and force on gases is the force of the firework on the gases - they involve three different objects so cannot be a pair.

B.explanation: Air resistance and thrust both act on the firework, but a third law pair must act on two different objects.

C.explanation: Force on gases is the firework pushing down on the gases and thrust is the gases pushing up on the firework - equal, opposite and on different objects.

D.explanation: Thrust is the gases on the firework and weight is the Earth on the firework - both act on the same object and are different types of force.

hints: Look at the diagram labels: thrust points up on the firework and force on gases points down on the expelled gases.
Recall a Newton's third law pair must be the same type of interaction, opposite in direction, and act on two different objects.
Ask which two forces are the two sides of the same firework-gases push, rather than forces involving the air or the Earth.
walkthrough: Identify the objects from the stem and diagram: the firework moves vertically up and pushes gases vertically down.
State the third law rule: if object X exerts a force on object Y, then Y exerts an equal and opposite force on X, so the two forces act on different objects.
Force on gases is the firework acting down on the gases. Thrust is the gases acting up on the firework.
These are opposite in direction, equal in size, same contact interaction type, and on different objects, so they satisfy all third law conditions.
Air resistance involves the air, and weight involves the Earth, so they cannot pair with the firework-gases forces. This is option C
